componentContentNotes.beb-stat2: Develops confidence intervals, tests of means, simple linear regression and correlation, checking model assumptions and good statistical practice.
componentContentNotes.beb-history: Studies long-run income and wealth inequality, market failures and government intervention, with economic-policy examples and information-literacy work.
componentContentNotes.beb-economics: Introduces economic models, strategic interaction, limited information, preferences and empirical evidence for understanding inequality and sustainability.
componentContentNotes.beb-public-admin: Studies public institutions, bureaucracies, policy making and the roles of government, companies and citizens in addressing societal problems.
componentContentNotes.beb-methods: Develops research objectives, questions and a feasible proposal using experimental, cross-sectional or case-study designs.
componentContentNotes.beb-macro-trade: Studies the open economy, inflation, unemployment, exchange rates, international trade and the effects of economic and trade-policy instruments.
componentContentNotes.beb-env-econ: Uses economics to analyse environmental degradation and the effectiveness and efficiency of policy instruments at local through global scales.
componentContentNotes.beb-food-systems: Compares economic schools of thought on food-system questions involving sustainability, social justice, power, workers and consumers.
componentContentNotes.beb-adv-stat: Studies regression, analysis of variance, categorical data, non-parametric tests and statistical designs, including analysis and interpretation using R.
componentContentNotes.beb-problem: Uses multidisciplinary problem-oriented study: an ethical research proposal, a literature or interview-based investigation, and written and oral reporting.
componentContentNotes.beb-econometrics: Combines economic theory, data and statistical estimation and testing to investigate relationships and answer social-science research questions.
componentContentNotes.beb-eu: Studies EU institutions, legal frameworks and policy processes, including political struggles over life-science and sustainability issues.
componentContentNotes.beb-micro: Develops mathematical and graphical models of consumers, producers, markets, uncertainty, asymmetric information and government-policy effects.
componentContentNotes.beb-growth: Uses growth models and empirical evidence to study differences in income, productivity, technology, institutions and economic development.
componentContentNotes.beb-linear: Applies vectors, matrices, linear systems, eigenvalues, iteration, projection and regression, including numerical software.
componentContentNotes.beb-change: Studies problem definition, agenda setting, decisions, implementation and evaluation as governance arrangements and policy change.
componentContentNotes.beb-inst-econ: Uses contemporary cases such as land tenure, futures markets and food supply chains to study institutions, incentives and economic organisation.
componentContentNotes.beb-public-sector: Studies government taxing and spending, efficiency and distribution, behavioural responses, public debt, social security and links with the EU.
componentContentNotes.beb-energy: Integrates economics and governance to analyse energy markets, externalities, distribution, stakeholder choices and policy interventions in energy transitions.
componentContentNotes.beb-industrial: Uses formal economic analysis of firm strategies, competition, market power and the role of public policy.
componentContentNotes.beb-math-choice: Example for entry with VWO Mathematics A: functions, equations, differentiation and integration in Mathematics Applied: Introduction. Students with VWO Mathematics B choose Statistics 1 instead.
componentContentNotes.beb-agri-food: Selected Economics-track option on agricultural and food-policy instruments, EU agricultural policy, international trade and rural development.
componentContentNotes.beb-regional: Selected Economics-track option on location, distance, firms, households and regional economic activity. The zero-credit Fieldwork Safety course is a mandatory prerequisite. General Safety is also required for new students and carries no credits.
componentContentNotes.beb-thesis: Twelve credits include a 1-credit Bachelor Assessment and an 11-credit individual thesis. The assessment, including reflection and a motivated study plan, must be passed before thesis writing. Entry requires at least 102 compulsory or restricted credits, including all first-year credits. Research includes a report, presentation and defence; current chair-specific preparation remains unconfirmed.
componentContentNotes.beb-science-choice: Twelve credits must be natural or life science courses agreed with the study adviser. The exact permitted package remains unverified.
componentContentNotes.beb-electives: Thirty credits remain genuinely open for a minor or elective courses after reserving the required science selection.
